x: E-KO RIP Center is a free, open-source wide-format printing RIP. A server installed on a Linux PC in the print shop receives the files, calculates the renders and drives the printers and cutters. Workstations connect to it with the Mac, Linux or Windows client ; the mobile app follows production; E-KO RIP Cloud gives access to the shop from outside. How the server, clients, machines, mobile app and Cloud fit together

All the work is done on the server. Clients send the files and show the queue; once a file has been sent, you can close the client: rendering and printing carry on. One server for the whole shop. Every workstation, Mac, Linux or Windows, sees the same queue and the same machines. The server stays in the shop. It is never exposed to the Internet; to reach it from outside, use E-KO RIP Cloud , which is free. Free software. x: Choose a 64-bit (x86) PC that will stay switched on, preferably with an SSD reserved for the data, connected by cable and on a UPS. Give it a fixed IP address on the router. Details: choosing the server PC .

The server is the heart of the RIP: it runs on Linux on a PC in the shop, receives the files from the workstations, calculates the renders and drives the machines. This page covers choosing the PC, installation, accounts and first start-up.

The server is the computer that must never stop. Rendering the files (Ghostscript) is the heaviest task. The E-KO RIP Center client is the software for the workstations: you use it to send files, follow the jobs and the queue, and start printing and cutting. It exists for Mac, Linux and Windows; all of them talk to the same server and see the same queue.

The window has three panes: on the left, the sidebar : Jobs , Machines , System ( Travaux , Machines , Système ); in the centre, the job table (name, folder, pages, status, date), with a search box; on the right, the inspector for the chosen job: preview, job ticket, ink plates, alerts and the actions Print ( Imprimer ), Retry ( Relancer ), TIFF proof ( Épreuve TIFF ) and Delete ( Supprimer ). The client window (here on Linux, interface in French): sidebar, job table, inspector of the chosen job You send a file by dragging it onto the window (or onto the Dock icon on Mac), or with the + Send (

The Mac client: sidebar, jobs and inspector Requirements : macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later, Apple Silicon or Intel Mac. Download the client: e-ko.rip/telecharger/mac ( .dmg file of the latest version). Open the .dmg and drag E-KO RIP Center into Applications . Launch the application. It is signed and checked by Apple: it opens with no warning. At first launch, macOS asks for access to the local network : accept, otherwise the server is not found. Updates : download the new version and replace the application. The server and the client are updated separately; a client slightly older than the server

At first launch, the connection screen looks for E-KO RIP servers on the local network by itself and lists them under Servers found on the network ( Serveurs trouvés sur le réseau ; name, address, version): one click is enough. Search again ( Rechercher à nouveau ) repeats the search (about 3 seconds). If nothing appears, enter the address under Enter an address ( Saisir une adresse ), for example 192.168.1.20:8640 . Discovery does not cross routers or VPNs. If the server has accounts, the client then asks for the name and password. The session lasts 12 hours. The client remembers the server.

If the server is linked to E-KO RIP Cloud , enter the site's address, for example https://atelier.platform.e-ko.rip , then sign in with your server account. With the Sign in to the cloud button ( Se connecter au cloud ; Mac and Linux clients), the client opens the browser so you can sign in to your Cloud account, then lists your sites: one click is enough.

A client talks to only one server at a time. To switch from one shop to another (or from the local network to the Cloud), use Change server… : the list offers the servers found and the address entered last time.

The E-KO RIP app lets you follow the shop from a phone: print queue, machine status, ink levels and alerts. It warns you as soon as a machine stops with an error, even when the phone is in your pocket. It works on iPhone and Android. Note The app is for monitoring . It sends no files and does not set up printing or cutting: those operations are still done from a workstation (see Clients ).

See the print queue of each machine, with the outputs in progress first. Start, pause, stop, retry or move an output to the front. Check the status of each machine: printing, cutting, idle, unreachable. Check the level of each ink and the length of media left on the roll. Read the history of the latest alerts. Receive notifications for errors, nearly empty ink or failed outputs.

The app will soon be available on the App Store and on Google Play. The download link and the news are announced on the app page: https://e-ko.rip/app/ . Note You do not need an E-KO account to install the app. It connects only to the shop's RIP server.
The app asks which RIP server to connect to. There are two cases: in the shop with the local address, or remotely with E-KO RIP Cloud.

The phone must be on the shop's Wi-Fi network. Open the app. In the Server field ( Serveur ), enter the address of the RIP server, for example http://192.168.1.20:8640 . This is the address used in the desktop clients (see Install the server ). Tap Continue ( Continuer ). If the server asks for an account, enter the user name and password, then tap Sign in ( Se connecter ). An Operator ( Opérateur ) account is enough to follow the queue and act on outputs. Accounts are managed in the server administration (see Run the server ). The name and password are kept in the phone's secure storage. The

The app has four tabs: Queue , Machines , Alerts and Settings ( File , Machines , Alertes , Réglages ).

The Queue tab The Queue tab lists the outputs of each machine. Outputs in progress and waiting come first, then the recently finished outputs. Each output has a status: In progress ( En cours ), Waiting ( En attente ), Suspended ( Suspendue ), Finished ( Terminée ), Failed ( Échec ) or Cancelled ( Annulée ). If an output fails, the error message is shown under it. The elapsed time and the estimated time are shown when they are known. To act on an output: Tap the output. Choose the action you want in the list. Confirm if the app asks you to. The actions offered depend on the output's status: Ou

The Machines tab The Machines tab shows one card per machine: the status: Printing ( En impression ), Cutting ( En découpe ), Idle ( En attente ) or Unreachable ( Injoignable ); the current output; the level of each ink, with low levels highlighted; the length of media left on the roll; the current alerts (cover open, end of roll…); the time of the last reading. The server polls the Epson machines about once a minute. The values shown are therefore at most a few moments old.
The Alerts tab The Alerts tab keeps the last 200 events: machine alerts, nearly empty ink, failed outputs, unreachable machine. A badge marks events not yet seen.

The Settings tab shows: the server, the user and the role ( Administrator or Operator ; Administrateur , Opérateur ); the notification switches; the Send a test notification button ( Envoyer une notification d'essai ); the Sign out button ( Se déconnecter ) and the app's version number; the Help / Documentation link ( Aide / Documentation ), which opens this page.
Notifications reach you even when the app is closed.

Accept the permission requested by the phone at first sign-in. Open the Settings tab and check that Notifications is on. Tap Send a test notification : it should arrive within a few seconds. In Settings , two switches define what you receive: Machine errors ( Erreurs machine ): alerts, ink, failures, unreachable machine. Print finished ( Fins d'impression ): a notification for every finished print. This option is off by default.

Event When Machine alert A new alert appears (cover open, media used up…). Ordinary states (ready, printing, warming up, starting up, standby) do not notify. The app shows the alert in French; a message the RIP does not know yet stays in the machine's own wording. Nearly empty ink An ink drops to 5% or less. Empty cartridge An ink reaches 0%. Machine unreachable Three readings in a row without an answer, then a notification when it answers again. Failed output A print or a cut fails. Failed render The render of a job fails. t: Which address should I enter to connect?
x: In the shop, the server's local address (for example http://192.168.1.20:8640 ). Away from the shop, the site's address on the cloud ( https://<site>.platform.e-ko.rip ) or the Sign in to the cloud button. See E-KO RIP Cloud .

t: The app cannot reach the server
x: Check that the phone is on the shop's Wi-Fi, if you are using the local address. Check the address you entered, with no spaces. Away from the shop, use the cloud: the local address can only be reached on site. If the problem persists, see Troubleshooting .

t: The site is "offline" in the list
x: The shop's RIP server is not linked to the platform: it is switched off or has no Internet. Check the server on site (see E-KO RIP Cloud ).
Check the permission in the phone's settings, the Notifications switch in Settings , then that the RIP server is up to date. Signing out and back in renews the registration.

t: Can I send a file to print from the phone?
x: No. Files are sent from a workstation or from the browser (see Install the clients ).

t: Why does printing carry on after Stop ?
x: Stop cancels a waiting or suspended output. A print that has already gone to the machine cannot be interrupted from the app.
Write to contact@e-ko.rip.

E-KO RIP Cloud gives access to the shop's RIP server from outside: from home, at a customer's site, on the road. It works with no VPN and without changing anything on the Internet router. The service is free for a small shop; paid plans cover larger shops. The shop's server connects to the platform; remote workstations and phones go through it

Without the Cloud, the RIP server can only be reached on the shop's network. With the Cloud: workstations (Mac, Linux, Windows) connect to the server from anywhere; the administration interface opens in a browser, just as in the shop; the mobile app follows production away from the shop; notifications and e-mails warn you when the server stops responding. The principle is simple: the shop's server itself opens a connection to the platform. No port has to be opened on the router. Remote workstations and phones go through the platform to reach the server. Note The Cloud is optional. The server k

The platform's portal is at https://platform.e-ko.rip . The portal sign-in page Open https://platform.e-ko.rip . Choose Create an account ( Créer un compte ). Enter the name (or the shop's name), the e-mail address and a password of at least 10 characters. Accept the terms of use, then confirm. If the page offers Google or Facebook , these buttons also let you sign up without a password.

A confirmation e-mail is sent when you sign up with a password. Open the e-mail sent by E-KO RIP Cloud ( no-reply@e-ko.fr ). Click the confirmation link, valid for 24 hours. Click the button on the page to confirm. Until the address is confirmed, a banner says so on My sites ( Mes sites ) and My account ( Mon compte ). It offers Resend the e-mail ( Renvoyer l'e-mail ). Linking a server is refused until the address is confirmed. The rest of the portal works. An account created with Google is confirmed automatically. Tip If the e-mail does not arrive, look in the spam folder, then ask for a new
Linking takes two steps: a code on the server, then entering that code on the portal. Allow two minutes.

The server must have at least one user account . Without an account, access to the server is open on the local network, and the Cloud refuses to open so as not to leave the shop open to everyone. To create an account, see Run the server . The server must also have Internet access (see Install the server ).

Open the RIP server's administration interface, with an administrator account. Go to System › E-KO RIP Cloud . Click Connect to the platform . The server shows a short code, such as KXRT-4821 , valid for 10 minutes . On the portal, sign in with your account. Go to My sites , section Link a RIP server ( Rattacher un serveur RIP ). Enter the code, then click Link ( Rattacher ). Entering the code in My sites Tip The server also shows a link: opening it leads straight to the code entry page. A few seconds later, the server is linked. The System › E-KO RIP Cloud screen shows Connected: reachable re
Each site has its own address: It is shown in System › E-KO RIP Cloud on the server, and in My sites on the portal. It is used in three cases.
Open the client (see Mac , Linux or Windows ). Enter the site's address in place of the server's local address. Sign in with an account of the RIP server.
Open the site's address. Sign in with an account of the RIP server. The administration interface works just as in the shop.

Enter the site's address in the Server field, or use Sign in to the cloud (see below). Details in Mobile app . Note The accounts used remotely are those of the RIP server, the ones in Run the server . The platform account is used for the portal and for Sign in to the cloud .

Open My account on the portal. Tick or untick Receive alerts and Receive the weekly summary ( Recevoir les alertes , Recevoir le résumé hebdomadaire ). Both boxes are ticked by default. A question, a problem, an idea? You can reach the E-KO support team from the portal, with no other account to create: click Support in the sidebar. My support requests

Click Support , then New request ( Nouvelle demande ). Choose the Queue ( File ): Technique (Technical), Comptabilité (Accounting), Commercial (Sales) or Idée (Idea). Enter the Subject ( Sujet ) and your message. Attach a screenshot or a log if needed: up to 5 files of 10 MB each. Click Send the request ( Envoyer la demande ). An e-mail confirms receipt, with the request reference ( TKT-… ). The request thread, the team's replies and a reply box are in Support , by clicking the request. A request thread

Every reply from the team arrives by e-mail and as a notification, with a link that opens the request directly. Reply from the page, not from the e-mail: the sending address ( no-reply ) does not read replies. The status shows in the list: Received ( Reçue ), In progress ( En cours ), Waiting for your reply ( En attente de votre réponse ), Resolved ( Résolue ) or Closed ( Fermée ). Replying to a resolved request reopens it. A closed request no longer takes messages: open a new request.

When the request is resolved, an e-mail offers to Rate the support ( Noter le support ). On the request page, pick a rating from 1 (not at all satisfied) to 5 (very satisfied), add a comment if you like, then click Send my rating ( Envoyer ma note ). You can change the rating later.

Choose the topic, write the first message, then click Start the chat ( Démarrer la discussion ). The team's messages appear in the bubble a few seconds after they are sent. Open My account . Go to the Delete my account section ( Supprimer mon compte ). Confirm. Warning Deletion erases the account, its rights and the sites it owns . Their remote access stops immediately. The shop's RIP server itself is not touched: it stays usable on site.

t: When the fleet exceeds the plan
x: When there are more sites or machines than the plan includes: An e-mail warns the owner and the site administrators. A 14-day grace period lets you subscribe to a suitable plan or remove the extra machines or sites. After that, remote access to the sites concerned is suspended until the situation is put right. Note Work in the shop is never affected: the RIP server keeps printing and cutting normally. Only remote access is suspended.

The RIP server can send the platform a backup of its configuration : it is the same archive as System › Backup (machines, settings, ICC profiles...). It contains neither jobs nor accounts . Backups are encrypted and hosted in France. When : every night (if the configuration changed), about 2 minutes after a change, and on demand by an administrator. How long : depending on the plan, the latest version (Free), 30 versions (Per machine), 90 days (Atelier) or 1 year (Pro). The most recent one is always kept. The site owner and administrators can restore from the portal. Open My sites , then the site's Backups . Find the version you want (date, reason, size). It can also be downloaded. Click Restore and confirm. The RIP server's configuration is replaced by that of the backup. With the Pro plan, a backup can also be restored to another site of the same owner. Warning A restore replaces the server's current configuration. If in doubt, download a backup of the current state first.

t: What never goes through the Cloud
x: Some functions stay reserved for the shop, even with the Cloud: the ERP bridge and its settings; forwarding jobs between two RIPs; linking and unlinking the Cloud itself: these are done only from the shop. The server refuses these requests when they arrive through the Cloud. For safety, it also refuses them when no account is declared on the server.

No port is open in the shop: the server connects to the platform, never the other way round. Each site has its own address, isolated from those of other sites and from the portal. An account's password is blocked for 5 minutes after 5 failures. The portal passes only the RIP server's session to the shop, never the platform account's information.

The shop's RIP server is not linked to the platform. Check on site that the server is switched on and has Internet access. Open System › E-KO RIP Cloud . The message Platform unreachable points to an Internet connection problem. Wait a minute: after an outage, the server reconnects by itself. If the alert is enabled, a "back online" e-mail confirms recovery.

t: The code has expired or is refused
x: The code is valid for only 10 minutes. On the server, click Connect to the platform again to get a new one. If the portal refuses the link, check that the account's e-mail address is confirmed.

t: The Cloud will not open: "at least one account"
x: Create an account on the server (see Run the server ), then try again.
Use Forgot your password? on the sign-in page (see above). For a RIP server account, see Run the server .

The plan has been exceeded for more than 14 days (too many machines or sites). Open Subscription : subscribing to a suitable plan or removing the extra machines restores access. Work in the shop was not interrupted.

t: I cannot find my online backups
x: They are in My sites › Backups . If the latest one is old, check that the site is online and that the plan's quota is not full.

t: I do not receive the e-mails

This page is for the person who looks after the server: accounts, backups, updates, shared folders and advanced settings. The commands are typed on the server, in a terminal or over SSH.

The log records every failed render and every failed output, with the machine, the job and the reason. In the client, the System view shows the version, the free disk space and how long jobs are kept. A restart interrupts the render in progress: the job goes to the "interrupted" failure state, to be restarted with Retry . Outputs in the queue stay in the queue; everyone reconnects.

Action Command Add an administrator sudo -u eko-rip env EKO_RIP_DATA=/var/lib/eko-rip eko-rip-serveur utilisateur ajouter <nom> admin Add an operator … utilisateur ajouter <nom> operateur List the accounts … utilisateur liste Delete an account … utilisateur supprimer <nom> Forgotten password or role change : declare the account again with utilisateur ajouter ; the new password and role replace the old ones. 5 wrong passwords block the name for 5 minutes. Deleting an account closes its sessions at once. No restart is needed.

The configuration (machines, media, prices, saved presets, cutting, spot colours, ICC profiles): in the client, Administration… › System › Configuration backup › Download the backup . Keep the file off the server, and make a new backup after every settings change. Everything, accounts included : copy the /var/lib/eko-rip folder, with the service stopped. Jobs are large and can be rebuilt from their source files: the configuration and the accounts file ( utilisateurs.json ) are often enough. Before every update , the package copies the configuration by itself into /var/lib/eko-rip/sauvegardes/

Install the server on the new PC ( Install the server ). Create the administrator account. In the client: System › Configuration backup › Restore… and choose the file. Everything is checked before anything is written: a damaged file changes nothing. Recreate the operator accounts.

Through the APT repository (server installed as recommended): The data stays in place. The administration interface comes from the server: new features appear there as soon as it is updated. The clients are updated separately (see Install the clients ). What is new in each version is in the release notes , with an e-mail subscription.

Each saved preset has a folder /var/lib/eko-rip/entrees/<preset>/ : a file dropped into it goes to the RIP with that preset. To drop files there from the workstations: Saved presets: each one has its own hot folder Add to the end of /etc/samba/smb.conf : Then sudo smbpasswd -a eko and sudo systemctl restart smbd . Workstations open smb://<server>/eko-rip (Mac, Linux) or \\<server>\eko-rip (Windows). Note Hot folders do not require a RIP account: access is controlled by the Samba share.

In /etc/default/eko-rip-serveur , then sudo systemctl restart eko-rip-serveur . Everything is in /var/lib/eko-rip : one folder per job ( travaux/ ), the queue ( file.json ), the machine catalogue ( machines.json ), the media, the presets, the accounts (hashed passwords), the ICC profiles and the hot folders ( entrees/ ). Each settings file keeps its previous version ( .prec ): after a power cut, the server picks it up by itself and reports it in System .

Anonymous statistics : the server and the clients send an installation signal (version, system), with no data from the shop or from the files. To stop it: untick System › Anonymous statistics (server), Système › Confidentialité (Mac; System › Privacy ) or Système › Ce poste (Linux; System › This computer ); or set EKO_TELEMETRIE=0 in /etc/default/eko-rip-serveur . Report a problem : Help menu (Mac; Aide ), main menu (Linux) or System › Bug reports in the administration. The title and description are published on GitHub: put nothing confidential in them. The most common situations, from connection to printing, with their cause and what to do. The exact message shown by the client or the interface is quoted in bold.

t: The client cannot find the server
x: Check that the server is running: systemctl status eko-rip-serveur on the server, or open http://<address>:8640 in a browser: the status page should appear. On Mac, allow local network access (System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network). Automatic discovery does not cross routers, VPNs or some guest Wi-Fi networks: enter the address under Enter an address ( 192.168.1.20:8640 ). A firewall on the server must let TCP port 8640 through (and UDP 5353 for discovery).

t: The browser only shows a status page
x: This is intended: inside the shop, the full interface is reserved for the clients. Use the client ( Administration… menu) or the site's address on the Cloud .
No account is declared: any computer on the network can do everything. Create an administrator account ( Creating the accounts ).

t: "Too many attempts for this user: try again in 5 minutes."
x: Five wrong passwords: this name is blocked for 5 minutes. Wait, or restart the service (which closes all sessions). Forgotten password: see Accounts .
The account is an operator : machines, media, prices, profiles, saved presets and backup are reserved for the administrator.
The file exceeds the limit (8 GB by default). Raise it with EKO_RIP_MAX_MO in /etc/default/eko-rip-serveur , then restart.

The message is in the job details (inspector) and in the server log. Common causes: password-protected or damaged PDF: save it again from the layout software; very large file that exceeds the render time limit (30 min by default, EKO_RIP_DELAI_S ); full disk: see the free space in System ; Permission denied on every render under Ubuntu 26.04: update the server (0.31.0 or later). Fonts that are not embedded and images with too little resolution are flagged as soon as the file is sent, in the job's alerts.

t: A very large format takes a long time
x: A page whose render would exceed 3 GB (for example a 1.6 × 3 m banner at 720 dpi) is rendered in strips then stitched back together: it takes longer, but there is nothing to set. Allow for the disk space.

Less than 20 GB is left. Delete old jobs, shorten the retention time ( EKO_RIP_CONSERVATION_JOURS ) or enlarge the data disk. Below 5 GB, the server itself deletes the oldest inactive jobs and refuses those that would not fit.
The reason is shown under the output, in the queue: machine switched off or unreachable, USB port missing, permission denied. Fix it, then Redo the output from the history.

t: "The printer reports an alert: printing stopped."
x: The printer has reported a blocking alert (cover open, empty cartridge…). Clear it on the machine, then Redo the output.

A spot colour in the file has no ink on the machine: rename it White or Metallic , convert it to CMYK or add it to the spot colour table ( System › Spot colours ), then restart the job. With a direct network connection, white and silver currently go through a machine with a Folder connection.

t: The cut is offset from the print
x: Make a test cut, measure the gap and enter it as the cutter's Offset X / Y ( System › Machines ). See also Kona registration .
An output is still waiting for this machine in the queue. Move it on or cancel it first.
Measure the real speed (m² per hour at the roll width) and enter it as the machine's Speed .

t: The app does not receive alerts
x: Check that notifications are allowed in the phone's settings, then the app's alert settings. Details: Mobile app .

t: The site is "offline" on the Cloud
x: The server can no longer reach the platform: check that it is switched on and has Internet access (outgoing HTTPS). It reconnects by itself within a minute of the network coming back. Details: E-KO RIP Cloud .

Use Report a problem… ( Signaler un problème… ) in the client: the report goes with the server log (masked) and a reference is shown. Or write to contact@e-ko.rip , giving the server version ( System view) and the exact message. The System view (Système): server and client versions, free disk space, renders in progress
The words of the screen and of the documentation, with their French equivalent (the one on the French screen and in the French documentation ). Each feature is described in usage .

Term In French Definition Job Travail One received file (PDF, SVG, TIFF, PNG, JPEG) with its request: settings, pages, rendered plates, ticket. Rendering Rendu Turning the file into ink plates (Ghostscript), done once on arrival; a print or a cut goes out again without rendering again. Preflight Pré-vérification Check on arrival: fonts not embedded, low-resolution images, cut paths, sizes. It warns, or refuses when the preset says so. Preset Réglage A named set of choices (resolution, media, white, cutting, registration…), applied when sending or by a hot folder. Hot folder Dossier surveillé S

Term In French Definition Plate Plaque 8-bit image of one ink (0 = full ink, 255 = no ink). Spot colour Ton direct Named colour in the PDF ( White , Silver , CutContour …), output on its own plate instead of being mixed into CMYK. Cut spot colour Ton de découpe Spot colour carrying the cut paths ( CutContour …); never printed. Spot colour table Table des tons directs Exact name, aliases and Lab colour of each spot colour, to convert or recognise it. White / Silver (metallic) Blanc / Argent The Epson's special inks, recognised by the spot colour name ( White , Metallic …). Underlay Sous-couche

Term In French Definition Media Support The printed material (vinyl, banner…), with its roll width, inks and modes. Loaded media Support chargé The media in the machine, read from the Epson or chosen by the operator. Roll width Laize Usable width of the roll. Bleed Fond perdu Image extended past the trim size, so a slightly off cut leaves no white. Grommet Œillet Grommet mark placed around the edge of a banner. Tiling Mosaïque A large visual split into pieces that fit the roll width. Panel Lé Vertical strip of a tiled job, at most as wide as the roll. Tile Tuile One piece of a tiling in column

Term In French Definition Path Tracé A line the cutter follows. Cut layer Couche de découpe The paths of one spot colour name, cut together with one cut setting. Cut setting Réglage de coupe Speed, force, acceleration, tool and pattern of a layer. Registration Repérage The cutter reading printed marks, to cut exactly where the print is. Marks / Frame Repères / Cadre Crosses or a frame (with a barcode for the Kona) printed around the image for registration. Auto contour Détourage automatique Cut path computed around the image. Cutting tolerance Tolérance de découpe Ink extended past the cut con

Term In French Definition Machine Machine Printer or cutter in the catalogue (System > Machines). Connection Connexion How the server reaches the machine: TCP network, serial, device, folder, IPP or forwarding. Direct driver Pilote direct The RIP builds the printer's data stream itself (the Epson's ESC/P2) and sends it. Folder connection Connexion Dossier Nothing is sent: the output is copied into sorties/<machine>/ . IPP IPP Network printing protocol (CUPS); the stream goes raw in a Print-Job.
